prompt: A maintainer releases `v2.0.0`, then `v2.1.0` with a fix. Consumers pinned to `@v2` should get the fix automatically. Which release strategy does that?
explanation: The documented strategy: cut `v2.1.0`, then move the `v2` tag to it, so `@v2` consumers receive the fix on their next run while anyone needing to freeze can still pin `@v2.0.0` or a SHA. Breaking changes are exactly what bumps the major.

options.text: Semver releases with a moving major tag that is re-pointed at each minor release
Only ever publishing full commit SHAs to consumers
Releasing fixes as new major versions
Tagging releases only on a schedule, never on demand
